title: apricity-data loader: carry beat, keep only the compiling person's warp markers
description:
## Intent
Libraries carry your warp markers, one person's at a time.

## Scope
- `crates/apricity-data/src/loader.rs` `marker_annotations`: copy `beat`; for markers named `warp` keep only those owned by the compiling identity (`Library::metadata().identity.sub`, or the identity passed in), dropping others' before building the manifest.
- `design/storage.md` §1: the Marker line shows `beat`.
- Loader integration test in `crates/apricity-data/tests/loader_integration.rs` for the "one person's grid" scenarios.

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-data --test loader_integration` and the library scenarios in `cargo test -p apricity-cli --test daw_cli`.

Commit: `feat(<this id>): library loader carries one person's warp markers`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
